adapt.authors: Bretz, F.; Koenig, F.; Brannath, W.; et al.
adapt.difference: designs confirmatory trials able to adapt mid-course; adaptation is a different lever from repetition count, which is the one we hold.
adapt.title: Adaptive designs for confirmatory clinical trials

agentbench.authors: Liu, X.; Yu, H.; Zhang, H.; et al.
agentbench.difference: evaluates LLMs as agents across tasks; a benchmark comparison between systems, not a powered test of one system's change.
agentbench.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents

aqp.difference: surveys approximate query processing; AQP trades accuracy for cost inside one query, while we trade re-executions for decisiveness across a comparison.
aqp.title: Approximate Query Processing: What is New and Where to Go?: A Survey on Approximate Query Processing

atoml.difference: surveys reproducibility in AI venues; a survey of practice, while we derive the sampling quantity that practice needs.
atoml.title: State of the Art: Reproducibility in Artificial Intelligence
atoml.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

attestation.authors: McKeen, F.; Alexandrovich, I.; Berenzon, A.; et al.
attestation.difference: defines a hardware instruction set for isolated execution; the mechanism that makes an execution attributable, while we ask how many such executions a verdict needs.
attestation.title: Innovative instructions and software model for isolated execution
attestation.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Workshop on Hardware and Architectural Support for Security and Privacy

audit.authors: Wang, W.; An, B.; Jiang, Y.
audit.difference: optimises spot-checking effort for crowdsourced grading quality; an allocation problem among items, while ours is how many repetitions decide one item's verdict.
audit.title: Optimal Spot-Checking for Improving the Evaluation Quality of Crowdsourcing: Application to Peer Grading Systems
audit.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

bandits.authors: Auer, P.; Cesa-Bianchi, N.; Freund, Y.; et al.
bandits.difference: analyses the nonstochastic multiarmed bandit; sequential allocation of effort, which we do not do — our budget is fixed in advance.
bandits.title: The Nonstochastic Multiarmed Bandit Problem

bft.authors: Lamport, L.; Shostak, R.; Pease, M.
bft.difference: states the Byzantine generals problem; agreement is reached by protocols, while our verifier decides by sampling repeated runs.
bft.title: The Byzantine Generals Problem
bft.venue: ACM Transactions on Programming Languages and Systems

bh1995.difference: controls the false discovery rate over many hypotheses; we control nothing across hypotheses and instead characterise one comparison's power in the budget.
bh1995.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
bh1995.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology

bigbench.authors: Srivastava, A.; Rastogi, A.; Rao, A.; et al.
bigbench.difference: quantifies capabilities beyond the imitation game; a broad capability benchmark, not a powered comparison of two systems.
bigbench.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and extrapolating the capabilities of language models

bootstrap.difference: introduces the bootstrap; the resampling method we use to build the intervals whose inversion gives decidability.
bootstrap.title: An Introduction to the Bootstrap

bouthillier.authors: Bouthillier, X.; Delaunay, P.; Bronzi, M.; et al.
bouthillier.difference: accounts for variance in ML benchmarks; variance accounting is the input to our curve, where the curve itself is the contribution.
bouthillier.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks

byk2001.difference: extends false-discovery control to dependent tests; dependence between re-executions is part of our node's dispersion term rather than a multiplicity setting.
byk2001.title: The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency

chainofver.authors: Dhuliawala, S.; Komeili, M.; Xu, J.; et al.
chainofver.difference: reduces hallucination by verifying generated claims in stages; an internal verification pass, which is a different budget from external re-execution.
chainofver.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models

clopperpearson.authors: Clopper, C. J.; Pearson, E. S.
clopperpearson.difference: gives exact binomial fiducial limits; an exact alternative to the interval we use, with a conservatism we do not need here.
clopperpearson.title: The Use of Confidence Or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial

concreteproblems.authors: Amodei, D.; Olah, C.; Steinhardt, J.; et al.
concreteproblems.difference: frames concrete research problems in AI safety; a research agenda where our contribution is one measurable sub-question inside verification.
concreteproblems.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety

conformalgentle.difference: introduces conformal prediction as distribution-free uncertainty quantification; a per-item guarantee, while our quantity is a per-node detectability under repetition.
conformalgentle.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification

conformalreg.authors: Lei, J.; G’Sell, M.; Rinaldo, A.; et al.
conformalreg.difference: gives distribution-free predictive inference for regression; prediction coverage is not the comparison we derive, which is between two verification rules.
conformalreg.title: Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression
conformalreg.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

conformalvalid.difference: establishes conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors; validity is a property of a predictor, and we study a test's power.
conformalvalid.title: Conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors

contamination.authors: Deng, C.; Zhao, Y.; Tang, X.; et al.
contamination.difference: investigates benchmark contamination; contamination shifts a metric's meaning, and we ask whether a shift is detectable at a given budget.
contamination.title: Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models

costsampling.authors: Agarwal, S.; Iyer, A. P.; Panda, A.; et al.
costsampling.difference: computes approximate answers within an error bound over large data; we ask whether a budget's verdict is decidable, not whether an approximation is accurate.
costsampling.title: Blink and it's done: interactive queries on very large data

costsensitive.difference: makes classifiers cost-sensitive by wrapping them in a meta-procedure; a cost-aware learning method, where our cost is verification effort.
costsensitive.title: MetaCost: a general method for making classifiers cost-sensitive
costsensitive.venue: Proceedings of the fifth ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining

cot.authors: Wei, J.; Wang, X.; Schuurmans, D.; et al.
cot.difference: elicits reasoning with chain-of-thought prompting; a capability result, not a statement about the number of runs a verdict needs.
cot.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

design.difference: prices information before it is bought; the same calculus applied to a different good, where the buyer sets the number of re-executions.
design.title: Information Value Theory
design.venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics

dkw.authors: Dvoretzky, A.; Kiefer, J.; Wolfowitz, J.
dkw.difference: gives the asymptotic minimax behaviour of the empirical distribution function; a limit statement where our object is a finite-budget interval.
dkw.title: Asymptotic Minimax Character of the Sample Distribution Function and of the Classical Multinomial Estimator

drlrepro.authors: Henderson, P.; Islam, R.; Bachman, P.; et al.
drlrepro.difference: shows deep RL results are sensitive to seeds; seed sensitivity motivates our dispersion term and we measure its effect on detection.
drlrepro.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning That Matters
drlrepro.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

dyba2006.authors: Dybå, T.; Kampenes, V. B.; Sjøberg, D. I. K.
dyba2006.difference: reviews statistical power in software-engineering experiments; we derive the same power object for a re-execution verification budget rather than for a treatment effect.
dyba2006.title: A systematic review of statistical power in software engineering experiments

effectsize.difference: tabulates effect sizes for behavioural-science power analysis; a reference for standardised effects, which we reformulate for verification nodes.
effectsize.title: Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences

ekiden.authors: Cheng, R.; Zhang, F.; Kos, J.; et al.
ekiden.difference: gives confidentiality-preserving smart contracts with attested execution; we study a verifier that repeats a nondeterministic pipeline instead of trusting one attested run.
ekiden.title: Ekiden: A Platform for Confidentiality-Preserving, Trustworthy, and Performant Smart Contracts
ekiden.venue: 2019 IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P)

evalharness.authors: Liang, P.; Bommasani, R.; Lee, T.; et al.
evalharness.difference: holistically evaluates language models across scenarios; a broad measurement programme where our object is one decision's power.
evalharness.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models

evalues.difference: calibrates and combines e-values; a different evidence currency, where we use the closed-form power of a mean test under repetition.
evalues.title: E-values: Calibration, combination and applications

extremevalue.difference: introduces extreme-value theory; tail modelling for maxima, where our object is a mean-shift comparison with a dispersion term.
extremevalue.title: Extreme Value Theory: An Introduction
extremevalue.venue: Springer Series in Operations Research and Financial Engineering

fisher1922.difference: lays the foundations of theoretical statistics; the estimation theory our effect-size coordinates presuppose.
fisher1922.title: On the mathematical foundations of theoretical statistics
fisher1922.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Containing Papers of a Mathematical or Physical Character

flicker.authors: McCune, J. M.; Parno, B. J.; Perrig, A.; et al.
flicker.difference: minimises the trusted computing base per execution; a smaller base changes what one run attests, not how many runs a metric needs.
flicker.title: Flicker: an execution infrastructure for tcb minimization

gaia.authors: Mialon, G.; Fourrier, C.; Swift, C.; et al.
gaia.difference: introduces a benchmark for general assistants; benchmark design, while we supply the sampling arithmetic a benchmark comparison needs.
gaia.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants

goalmisspec.authors: Langosco, L.; Koch, J.; Sharkey, L.; et al.
goalmisspec.difference: studies goal misgeneralisation in reinforcement learning; a failure of objectives, where we study the cost of detecting a metric divergence.
goalmisspec.title: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning

groupseq.difference: fixes group-sequential boundaries for clinical trials under a planned effect size; we take the effect size as the unknown and ask which nodes a budget can decide.
groupseq.title: Group sequential methods in the design and analysis of clinical trials

hitchhiker.authors: Dror, R.; Baumer, G.; Shlomov, S.; et al.
hitchhiker.difference: guides significance testing in NLP; guidance on practice, while we give the closed-form budget-to-power relation practice would need.
hitchhiker.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
hitchhiker.venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

hochberg1988.difference: sharpens the Bonferroni step-up procedure; a multiplicity correction is orthogonal to the repetition budget we vary.
hochberg1988.title: A sharper Bonferroni procedure for multiple tests of significance

impossibility.authors: Bahadur, R. R.; Savage, L. J.
impossibility.difference: proves no nonparametric procedure is uniformly consistent on all alternatives; that is why our construct is stated as a curve over node dispersion rather than a uniform guarantee.
impossibility.title: The Nonexistence of Certain Statistical Procedures in Nonparametric Problems

ingster.authors: Ingster, Y. I.; Suslina, I. A.
ingster.difference: characterises the separation rate at which nonparametric tests can detect a departure; we measure detection for a specific mean-shift node class inside a verification budget.
ingster.title: Nonparametric Goodness-of-Fit Testing Under Gaussian Models

instructgpt.authors: Ouyang, L.; Wu, J.; Jiang, X.; et al.
instructgpt.difference: trains models to follow instructions from human feedback; a training method, upstream of the verification question we study.
instructgpt.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

judgebias.authors: Wang, P.; Li, L.; Chen, L.; et al.
judgebias.difference: finds LLM evaluators biased in position and format; evaluator bias shifts a node's mean, which is exactly the coordinate our curve reads.
judgebias.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators

landemets.authors: Gordon Lan, K. K.; Demets, D. L.
landemets.difference: gives discrete sequential boundaries for clinical trials; a boundary rule that assumes a planned effect, across which we instead measure decidability.
landemets.title: Discrete sequential boundaries for clinical trials

leaderboard.authors: Singh, S.; Nan, Y.; Wang, A.; et al.
leaderboard.difference: analyses leaderboard dynamics and rank instability; rank instability is a comparative symptom of the variance we model directly.
leaderboard.title: The Leaderboard Illusion

llmjudge.authors: Zheng, L.; Chiang, W. L.; Sheng, Y.; et al.
llmjudge.difference: shows LLM judges correlate with human preference; a judge is a scorer, and we ask how many re-executions make a scorer's comparison decidable.
llmjudge.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena

massart.difference: gives the tight constant in the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality; a tight constant sharpens intervals, which we use rather than derive.
massart.title: The Tight Constant in the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz Inequality

massey.difference: introduces the Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit test; a distributional test, where our comparison is between two rules' expected decisions.
massey.title: The Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test for Goodness of Fit
massey.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

mcmcse.authors: Flegal, J. M.; Jones, G. L.
mcmcse.difference: estimates Monte Carlo standard errors; the same estimation problem for a single sampler, applied here to a metric comparison across runs.
mcmcse.title: Implementing MCMC: Estimating with Confidence
mcmcse.venue: Handbook of Markov Chain Monte Carlo

metricsat.authors: Ott, S.; Barbosa-Silva, A.; Blagec, K.; et al.
metricsat.difference: maps benchmark creation and saturation dynamics; the saturation we measure is of a rule's advantage in the budget, not of a benchmark's headroom.
metricsat.title: Mapping global dynamics of benchmark creation and saturation in artificial intelligence

mltesting.authors: Zhang, J. M.; Harman, M.; Ma, L.; et al.
mltesting.difference: surveys machine-learning testing; a survey of testing practice where our contribution is the sampling arithmetic of one test family.
mltesting.title: Machine Learning Testing: Survey, Landscapes and Horizons

mmlu.authors: Hendrycks, D.; Burns, C.; Basart, S.; et al.
mmlu.difference: measures multitask language understanding; a benchmark whose scores would be compared under exactly the variance structure we quantify.
mmlu.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding

neuripsrepro.authors: Pineau, J.; Vincent-Lamarre, P.; Sinha, K.; et al.
neuripsrepro.difference: reports a conference reproducibility programme's findings; programme-level practice, where we quantify a single verifier's detection power.
neuripsrepro.title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research (A Report from the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program)

neymanpearson.difference: founds the most efficient test of a statistical hypothesis; the power framework our closed form instantiates for a re-execution budget.
neymanpearson.title: IX. On the problem of the most efficient tests of statistical hypotheses
neymanpearson.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Containing Papers of a Mathematical or Physical Character

notary.authors: Athalye, A.; Belay, A.; Kaashoek, M. F.; et al.
notary.difference: builds a device for secure transaction approval; the approval is a single attestation, where we price repetition.
notary.title: Notary: a device for secure transaction approval
notary.venue: Proceedings of the 27th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles

nova.difference: builds tamper-evident, replayable evidence for agent runs; an evidence substrate, where we study how many re-executions a policy-pinned metric needs before a verdict is decidable.
nova.title: NovaFabric: Tamper-Evident, Replayable Evidence for Autonomous AI Agent Runs

onlineagg.authors: Hellerstein, J. M.; Haas, P. J.; Wang, H. J.
onlineagg.difference: gives online aggregation with running confidence intervals; an interval over a query statistic, where our interval decides a rule comparison.
onlineagg.title: Online aggregation

optdesign.authors: Atkinson, A. C.; Donev, A. N.; Tobias, R. D.
optdesign.difference: treats optimum experimental design; optimal allocation of a fixed design budget, which is the closest classical analogue of our question and assumes a known model.
optdesign.title: Optimum Experimental Designs, with SAS

orderstats.authors: David, H. A.; Nagaraja, H. N.
orderstats.difference: gives the theory of order statistics; the distributional machinery behind the quantile-based quantities our intervals use.
orderstats.title: Order Statistics
orderstats.venue: Wiley Series in Probability and Statistics

outlierexposure.authors: Hendrycks, D.; Mazeika, M.; Dietterich, T.
outlierexposure.difference: trains anomaly detectors with outlier exposure; improves a detector's accuracy, which enters our curve as a dispersion coordinate.
outlierexposure.title: Deep Anomaly Detection with Outlier Exposure

passk.authors: Chen, M.; Tworek, J.; Jun, H.; et al.
passk.difference: evaluates code models with pass@k; pass@k measures capability growth with attempts, whereas our budget buys detection power, not capability.
passk.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

pbft.difference: makes Byzantine replication practical; replication assumes faulty replicas, and we assume honest re-executions of a nondeterministic pipeline.
pbft.title: Practical byzantine fault tolerance and proactive recovery

peeking.authors: Johari, R.; Koomen, P.; Pekelis, L.; et al.
peeking.difference: shows why peeking at A/B tests inflates error rates; peeking inflates the error rate, while our non-monotonicity is in the comparison between rules and in the construct's own approximation error.
peeking.title: Peeking at A/B Tests: Why it matters, and what to do about it
peeking.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining

peng2011.difference: argues for reproducible research in computational science; we measure what a verifier can conclude when it re-runs rather than reads.
peng2011.title: Reproducible Research in Computational Science

permutationtests.difference: treats permutation, parametric and bootstrap tests of hypotheses; a comparison of test families, where we compare two verification rules.
permutationtests.title: Permutation, Parametric and Bootstrap Tests of Hypotheses

pinocchio.authors: Parno, B.; Howell, J.; Gentry, C.; et al.
pinocchio.difference: makes verifiable computation practical; practical proving is an alternative to repetition, and we measure the repetition lever on its own.
pinocchio.title: Pinocchio: Nearly Practical Verifiable Computation
pinocchio.venue: 2013 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

power.difference: gives the conventional closed form for detecting a standardised mean difference; we give the same form for a re-execution budget and then measure where its band actually sits.
power.title: A power primer

propertytesting.authors: Goldreich, O.; Goldwasser, S.; Ron, D.
propertytesting.difference: relates property testing to learning and approximation; the sublinear-in-size logic is complementary to our sublinear-in-repeats question.
propertytesting.title: Property testing and its connection to learning and approximation

provdb.authors: Cheney, J.; Chiticariu, L.; Tan, W. C.
provdb.difference: surveys provenance in databases; provenance records what happened in one execution, whereas our verifier compares metrics across executions.
provdb.title: Provenance in Databases: Why, How, and Where

pvalues.authors: Greenland, S.; Senn, S. J.; Rothman, K. J.; et al.
pvalues.difference: warns against misinterpreting p-values, intervals and power; a misinterpretation guide whose power quantity we make budget-explicit.
pvalues.title: Statistical tests, P values, confidence intervals, and power: a guide to misinterpretations

qbc.authors: Seung, H. S.; Opper, M.; Sompolinsky, H.
qbc.difference: selects informative examples by committee disagreement; an active-sampling result, and our verifier samples uniformly rather than selectively.
qbc.title: Query by committee
qbc.venue: Proceedings of the fifth annual workshop on Computational learning theory

quantiles.difference: describes sample quantile conventions in statistical packages; a convention we rely on when reading quantile thresholds, not a claim we extend.
quantiles.title: Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages

recsyeval.authors: Ferrari Dacrema, M.; Cremonesi, P.; Jannach, D.
recsyeval.difference: questions progress claims in neural recommendation; a critique of comparisons that our power curve explains in sampling terms.
recsyeval.title: Are we really making much progress? A worrying analysis of recent neural recommendation approaches
recsyeval.venue: Proceedings of the 13th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems

redteam.authors: Perez, E.; Huang, S.; Song, F.; et al.
redteam.difference: generates adversarial test cases with language models; test generation finds failures, while our test decides whether a metric change is detectable.
redteam.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models

reportscores.difference: shows score distributions matter for LSTM tagging comparisons; reporting distributions is descriptive and we ask what conclusion a reader may draw.
reportscores.title: Reporting Score Distributions Makes a Difference: Performance Study of LSTM-networks for Sequence Tagging
reportscores.venue: Proceedings of the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

rewardoveropt.authors: Gao, L.; Schulman, J.; Hilton, J.
rewardoveropt.difference: gives scaling laws for reward-model overoptimisation; an empirical scaling law in a different coordinate, which inspired our curve's shape but not its derivation.
rewardoveropt.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization

robustopt.difference: surveys robust optimisation methodology; robustification changes the objective, where repetition changes the evidence for an objective comparison.
robustopt.title: Robust optimization – methodology and applications

roc.authors: Hanley, J. A.; McNeil, B. J.
roc.difference: explains the area under the ROC curve; a discrimination summary whose measurement variance follows the same repetition logic.
roc.title: The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve

runtimeverif.authors: Bartocci, E.; Falcone, Y.; Francalanza, A.; et al.
runtimeverif.difference: introduces runtime verification of executions against monitors; monitors judge traces, while we judge a metric comparison across repeated runs.
runtimeverif.title: Introduction to Runtime Verification

safetycase.authors: Graydon, P. J.; Holloway, C. M.
safetycase.difference: quantifies confidence in assurance arguments; we quantify the power of a re-execution comparison used as one premise of such an argument.
safetycase.title: An investigation of proposed techniques for quantifying confidence in assurance arguments

samplingverify.authors: Legay, A.; Delahaye, B.; Bensalem, S.
samplingverify.difference: surveys statistical model checking; we derive the budget-to-power mapping that a statistical model checker's parameters imply.
samplingverify.title: Statistical Model Checking: An Overview

selective.difference: lets a classifier abstain under a risk target; abstention is one model's decision, and our rule is a verifier's decision to ask for more runs.
selective.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks

selfconsistency.authors: Wang, X.; Wei, J.; Schuurmans, D.; et al.
selfconsistency.difference: improves reasoning by sampling several chains and voting; sampling is spent on agreement, where we spend it on detecting a divergence.
selfconsistency.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models

selfrefine.authors: Madaan, A.; Tandon, N.; Gupta, P.; et al.
selfrefine.difference: iterates refinement with self-feedback; iteration improves output, while we price repeated measurement of an already-fixed pipeline.
selfrefine.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

showyourwork.authors: Dodge, J.; Gururangan, S.; Card, D.; et al.
showyourwork.difference: improves reporting of experimental results across runs; reporting variance is the descriptive act, and we price the runs it would take to decide.
showyourwork.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
showyourwork.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP)

snarkc.difference: shrinks pairing-based arguments; argument size and repetition count are two different costs of verification, and we quantify the second.
snarkc.title: On the Size of Pairing-Based Non-interactive Arguments

spectre.authors: Kocher, P.; Horn, J.; Fogh, A.; et al.
spectre.difference: shows speculative execution leaks across isolation boundaries; attacker modelling is upstream of our question, which is about the verifier's own sampling budget.
spectre.title: Spectre Attacks: Exploiting Speculative Execution
spectre.venue: 2019 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)

student1908.difference: gives the probable error of a mean; the small-sample mean problem whose modern form we apply to repeated re-executions.
student1908.title: The Probable Error of a Mean

swebench.authors: Jimenez, C. E.; Yang, J.; Wettig, A.; et al.
swebench.difference: evaluates models on real GitHub issues; an execution-grounded benchmark whose variance is the kind our dispersion term describes.
swebench.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?

threshold.difference: bounds trustless verification of nondeterministic workflows by a threshold choice; we derive and measure the whole detection-power curve in the budget, including where extra re-executions buy nothing.
threshold.title: Threshold Choice, Not Sample Size, Bounds Trustless Verification of Nondeterministic Compound AI Workflows

timeuniform.authors: Howard, S. R.; Ramdas, A.; McAuliffe, J.; et al.
timeuniform.difference: builds time-uniform Chernoff bounds from supermartingales; uniform validity over time, where we measure the non-uniform band in which a budget changes a verdict.
timeuniform.title: Time-uniform Chernoff bounds via nonnegative supermartingales

tost.difference: compares two one-sided tests with the power approach for equivalence; equivalence testing is a different decision, where we ask whether an advantage is certifiable.
tost.title: A comparison of the Two One-Sided Tests Procedure and the Power Approach for assessing the equivalence of average bioavailability

tsybakov.difference: gives the theory of nonparametric estimation, including separation rates; we instantiate one separation question as a verifier's budget decision.
tsybakov.title: Introduction to Nonparametric Estimation

underspec.authors: D'Amour, A.; Heller, K.; Moldovan, D.; et al.
underspec.difference: shows underspecification makes ML results brittle across pipeline choices; brittleness across pipelines is the heterogeneity our node population samples.
underspec.title: Underspecification Presents Challenges for Credibility in Modern Machine Learning

valiant.difference: founds learnability in a distribution-free setting; a separability idealisation that a finite re-execution budget does not reach.
valiant.title: A theory of the learnable

vanderVaart.difference: gives asymptotic statistics for estimators and tests; asymptotics are the limit our measured band approaches as the budget grows.
vanderVaart.title: Asymptotic Statistics

vc1971.authors: Vapnik, V. N.; Chervonenkis, A. Y.
vc1971.difference: introduces the uniform convergence of relative frequencies; the concentration family our interval-based decidability rests on.
vc1971.title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events to Their Probabilities

verifiablecompute.authors: Gennaro, R.; Gentry, C.; Parno, B.
verifiablecompute.difference: outsources computation with correctness proofs; proofs make one execution checkable, whereas our verifier re-runs rather than proves.
verifiablecompute.title: Non-interactive Verifiable Computing: Outsourcing Computation to Untrusted Workers

wald.difference: introduces sequential tests that stop early on a likelihood ratio; designed for a known alternative, while our measured object is the power curve over an unknown node's dispersion.
wald.title: Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses

wilson.difference: gives an interval for a binomial proportion; the interval family used for the registration's rate quantities.
wilson.title: Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference
wilson.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

zeroshotreason.authors: Kojima, T.; Gu, S. S.; Reid, M.; et al.
zeroshotreason.difference: shows zero-shot reasoning is elicitable by prompting; capability, where our quantity is detectability under repetition.
zeroshotreason.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners

zkcnn.authors: Chen, B. J.; Waiwitlikhit, S.; Stoica, I.; et al.
zkcnn.difference: optimises ML inference inside zero-knowledge proofs; a proof-based route to trust that bypasses the statistical route we analyse.
zkcnn.title: ZKML: An Optimizing System for ML Inference in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
zkcnn.venue: Proceedings of the Nineteenth European Conference on Computer Systems

zktraining.authors: Garg, S.; Goel, A.; Jha, S.; et al.
zktraining.difference: proves training runs in zero knowledge; that certifies a computation happened, while our question is whether a re-execution comparison can detect a divergence.
zktraining.title: Experimenting with Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Training
zktraining.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
